meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Winning isn't a sometime thing; it's an all the time thing'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuinely Lombardi's — it opens his "What It Takes to Be Number One" speech. But no dated transcript or audio survives, so we call it attributed, not verified.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: This is genuinely Lombardi’s sentence, not one of the fakes: it opens What It Takes to Be Number One, the speech his family publishes in full on the official Vince Lombardi site ↗, and Wikiquote’s editors single it out as “something he did say.” What is missing is a pin: the estate’s text carries no date, occasion or citation, no recording of the speech is known to survive, and we could not tie the wording to a dated contemporaneous transcript — so we log it as attributed rather than verified.

source.excerpt: Winning is not a sometime thing; it’s an all the time thing. You don’t win once in a while; you don’t do things right once in a while; you do them right all of the time. Winning is a habit. Unfortunately, so is losing.
trail: Wikiquote ↗ does not give this line its own sourced entry. It appears inside the note under the Misattributed heading for “Winning isn’t everything; it’s the only thing,” where editors write that Lombardi “always denied he had said this although it is close to something he did say: ‘Winning isn’t a sometime thing; it’s an all the time thing.’”

The Lombardi family’s official site ↗ prints the sentence as the opening of What It Takes to Be Number One and repeats a shortened form on its quotes page — in both places without a date, venue or citation.

Speakola ↗ reproduces the same text, credits it to vincelombardi.com, files it under “1961, Green Bay, Wisconsin,” and adds the caution that there is no surviving audio of the speech — the voice in the popular video is an actor doing a paraphrase.

Steven J. Overman’s peer-reviewed study in Football Studies (October 1999), held by the LA84 Foundation ↗, lists “Winning is not a sometime thing. It is an all-the-time thing” in a footnote among Lombardi’s own quotes on winning — genuine, but without a discrete citation of its own.
source.excerptNote: As published by the Family of Vince Lombardi. The popular one-line form contracts “is not” to “isn’t” and stops after the first sentence — which is why the second half, the part that actually explains the line, is almost never quoted.

author.name: Vince Lombardi
author.heading: Who was Vince Lombardi?
author.metaLine: 1913–1970 · NFL head coach, Green Bay Packers and Washington
author.bio: Vincent Thomas Lombardi (June 11, 1913 – September 3, 1970) coached at St. Cecilia High School, Fordham and West Point before running the New York Giants’ offense from 1954 to 1958. As head coach of the Green Bay Packers from 1959 to 1967 he won five NFL championships in seven years, including the first two Super Bowls, and he returned to the sideline in Washington in 1969. His off-season speaking career made him the most-quoted coach in America — and, because so much of that speaking survives only as text passed hand to hand, one of the most loosely quoted.

misattribution.heading: What goes wrong with this one
misattribution.intro: Nobody steals this line from Lombardi — it goes wrong in three quieter ways: it gets swapped for a quote that isn’t his, its wording drifts, and at least one large aggregator has filed it under the wrong Lombardi.

items.why: Ask most people for Lombardi’s line about winning and you get “Winning isn’t everything; it’s the only thing.” Quote Investigator ↗ ascribes that one to 1950s UCLA coach Henry Russell “Red” Sanders, and Wikiquote ↗ files it under Misattributed — noting Lombardi “always denied he had said this although it is close to something he did say”: the “sometime thing” sentence.

Goodreads ↗ files a copy of the quote under Vince Lombardi Jr., the coach’s son, rather than the coach. The son edited and republished his father’s material, which is very likely how the credit slid one generation down.

The estate’s own text reads “Winning is not a sometime thing; it’s an all the time thing” on vincelombardi.com ↗, while its quotes page renders the same idea as “Winning is not a sometime thing, it is an all the time thing. You don’t do things right once in a while…you do them right all the time.” Elsewhere it becomes “an all-time thing” — the form LibQuotes ↗ prints. The popular “Winning isn’t a sometime thing” is a contraction of the estate’s “is not.”

misattribution.truthLine: The thought and the phrasing are Lombardi’s — the Lombardi family ↗ publish it as the opening of What It Takes to Be Number One — but the speech comes to us as an undated text with no surviving recording, so we credit it to him without claiming a source we cannot show you.

context.heading: Why this one keeps getting tangled up
lead: Lombardi has two famous sentences about winning, and the public keeps merging them. One is “Winning isn’t everything; it’s the only thing” — the one he is most often credited with, the one Quote Investigator ↗ traces to UCLA coach Red Sanders, and the one Lombardi later tried to walk back. The other is this one, which is his, and which almost nobody can source.

That asymmetry is the whole story of the page. The Sanders line has been chased through newspapers, a 1953 Hollywood script and two chapters of David Maraniss’s biography. “Winning is not a sometime thing” has had no comparable investigation — it simply appears, fully formed, at the top of a speech text that the Lombardi family publishes and that Speakola ↗ reproduces with the blunt editorial note that no audio of the speech survives at all.
detailsBody: Steven J. Overman’s 1999 article in Football Studies is the closest thing to a scholarly audit. It documents that Lombardi opened the Packers’ 1959 training camp with the “only thing” formulation, that he later offered an apologia — “I have been quoted as saying, ‘Winning is the only thing’. That’s a little out of context” — and it lists “Winning is not a sometime thing. It is an all-the-time thing” in a footnote among his other statements on winning, without assigning it a discrete source.

The speech text itself contains an internal clue about its earliest possible date: Lombardi says he has “finished second twice in my time at Green Bay,” which places the version we have somewhere inside his Packers tenure. That is an observation about the text, not a documented date, and we have not used it to fix one.
context.pull: His most quotable line about consistency is the one nobody has managed to date.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Vince Lombardi page, in the note under the Misattributed entry for "Winning isn't everything; it's the only thing," states that quote was "Actually spoken by 1950s UCLA football coach Henry Russell 'Red' Sanders. Lombardi always denied he had said this although it is close to something he did say: 'Winning isn't a sometime thing; it's an all the time thing.'"

Quote Investigator ascribes "Winning isn't everything; it's the only thing" to Henry 'Red' Sanders rather than Lombardi, and cites a November 1962 Esquire item quoting Lombardi as "Winning isn't everything, but wanting to win is!"

The official Vince Lombardi site publishes "What It Takes to be Number One" opening with "Winning is not a sometime thing; it's an all the time thing…", gives no date or citation for it, and carries the footer "© 2026 Family of Vince Lombardi c/o Luminary Group LLC" with licensing directed to Luminary Group.

The Vince Lombardi site's quotes page lists, under Commitment, "Winning is not a sometime thing, it is an all the time thing. You don't do things right once in a while…you do them right all the time." with no source attribution.

Speakola publishes the speech under the heading '"Winning is not a sometime thing; it's an all the time thing" - 1961', labels it "1961, Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA", sources the text to vincelombardi.com, and states "The voice in the YouTube clip above is an actor doing a paraphrase of the speech below… There is no surviving audio of it."

Steven J. Overman, "'Winning Isn't Everything. It's the Only Thing': The Origin, Attributions and Influence of a Famous Football Quote," Football Studies vol. 2 no. 2 (October 1999), pp. 77–99, lists "Winning is not a sometime thing. It is an all-the-time thing" among Lombardi's other quotes on winning, and documents that Lombardi's 1959 Packers training-camp talk used "Winning isn't everything, it's the only thing" and that he later said "I have been quoted as saying, 'Winning is the only thing'. That's a little out of context."

Wikipedia's article on "Winning isn't everything; it's the only thing" attributes the phrase to UCLA coach Red Sanders, notes it was quoted in the 1953 film Trouble Along the Way, and says the quotation is widely but wrongly attributed to Vince Lombardi, citing Maraniss's biography.
Goodreads files the quote "Winning is not a sometime thing; it's an all time thing…" under the author name Vince Lombardi Jr. rather than Vince Lombardi.

LibQuotes prints the variant "Winning is not a sometime thing. It's an all-time thing." and sources it to "'What It Takes to be Number One', speech, quoted in Vince Lombardi Jr, What It Takes To Be Number One (2012)".
